description: Key facts a correct lesson on each Geotechnical Engineering topic must state. Every fact was taken from the fetched text of the source page named with it (the quote is checked by `npm run golden:check`). Patterns are case-insensitive regular expressions matched against the lesson text after LaTeX backslashes and braces are removed.
subject: geotechnical-engineering

facts.claim: Soil is solids plus pore water and air (a three-phase system)

source.quote: soils consist of a heterogeneous mixture of fluids (usually air and water) and particles

facts.claim: Shrinkage, plastic and liquid limits are critical water contents

source.quote: The Atterberg limits are a basic measure of the critical water contents of a fine-grained soil

facts.claim: Liquid limit: water content where soil changes from plastic to liquid

source.quote: The liquid limit (LL) is conceptually defined as the water content at which the behavior of a clayey soil changes from the plastic state to the liquid state

facts.claim: USCS uses two-letter symbols (e.g. GW, SP, CL)

source.quote: is represented by a two-letter symbol

facts.claim: Darcy's law: flow ∝ hydraulic gradient (v = k i)

source.quote: linearly relating the volume flow rate of the fluid to the hydraulic head difference

facts.claim: Based on experiments with water through sand

source.quote: based on results of experiments on the flow of water through beds of sand

facts.claim: Effective stress is the part carried by the soil skeleton (σ' = σ − u)

source.quote: describes the portion of total stress in a soil mass that is carried by the solid soil skele

facts.claim: It controls strength and volume change

source.quote: effective stress governs both their strength and volume change

facts.claim: Flow lines and equipotential lines cross at right angles

source.quote: stream and equipotential lines, which are everywhere perpendicular to each other

facts.claim: Compaction densifies soil by expelling air

source.quote: stress applied to a soil causes densification as air is displaced from the pores

facts.claim: Gives maximum dry density at the optimum moisture content

source.quote: the maximum dry density and the optimum moisture content are vital

facts.claim: Consolidation: volume decreases slowly as pore water drains

source.quote: As water diffuses away from regions of high pressure due to seepage, the soil matrix gradually takes up the pressure change and shrinks in volume

facts.claim: τ = c + σ tan φ (cohesion and friction angle)

source.quote: is often called the cohesion and the angle

facts.claim: Triaxial test: cylindrical sample with confining pressure and axial stress

source.quote: applying fluid pressure to the specimen

facts.claim: Factor of safety = shear strength / shear stress; < 1 means unstable

source.quote: If the value of factor of safety is less than 1.0, the slope is unstable

facts.claim: Lateral earth pressure is the horizontal soil pressure on walls

source.quote: The lateral earth pressure is the pressure that soil exerts in the horizontal direction

facts.claim: Active pressure (Ka) when the wall moves away from the soil

source.quote: the active earth pressure is obtained, for example, when a retaining wall moves away from the soil

facts.claim: Maximum contact pressure without shear failure of the soil

source.quote: the maximum average contact pressure between the foundation and the soil which should not produce shear failure in the soil

facts.claim: Depends on soil shear strength and foundation size, shape and depth

source.quote: It depends upon the shear strength of soil as well as shape, size, depth and type of foundation
